Gene set enrichment on sc-ExWAS results

Source: R/enrichment.R
run_gsea.Rd

Runs fast gene set enrichment analysis (fgsea) on the ranked gene list from run_sc_exwas, separately for each cell type and exposure.

Usage

run_gsea(
  exwas_result,
  gene_sets,
  rank_by = "statistic",
  min_size = 10L,
  max_size = 500L
)

Arguments

exwas_result

A DataFrame returned by run_sc_exwas or run_multi_exwas.

gene_sets

A named list of character vectors, one gene set each. The genes are named as in the gene column of exwas_result, which holds the row names of the object that was analysed: Ensembl identifiers when the rows are Ensembl identifiers, symbols when they are symbols.

rank_by

Character scalar naming the numeric column used to rank genes. Default "statistic", whose scale depends on the sc-ExWAS backend: signed square-root QL F for edgeR, Wald statistic for DESeq2, and moderated t statistic for voom-dream. "log2FC" ranks by effect size; any other numeric column of exwas_result may be named.

min_size

Integer. Minimum gene set size. Default 10.

max_size

Integer. Maximum gene set size. Default 500.

Value

A DataFrame with the fgsea columns pathway, pval, padj (within cell type and exposure), log2err, ES, NES, size and leadingEdge (semicolon-separated), plus celltype, exposure and padj_global (Benjamini-Hochberg across all cell types and exposures).

Details

This function requires the fgsea package (Bioconductor). Gene sets can come from any source, for example from MSigDB via msigdbr::msigdbr(), as long as they use the identifiers of the result.

Genes are ranked by the backend-specific association statistic (default) within each cell type, then fgsea is run per cell type. For edgeR QL this is the signed square root of the QL F statistic and is not a Wald z statistic. Results are combined with a final cross-cell-type FDR adjustment.

Ranking by the signed statistic preserves direction and within-backend evidence ordering. Statistic magnitudes are not calibrated for comparison across different backends; use rank_by = "log2FC" when an effect-size ranking is the scientific target.

fgsea estimates p-values by Monte Carlo sampling, so they depend on the random number generator state. run_gsea() runs fgsea serially, so calling set.seed() beforehand makes them reproducible. When a gene appears more than once in a stratum, its largest ranking value is kept.

References

Korotkevich G et al. (2021). Fast gene set enrichment analysis. bioRxiv. doi:10.1101/060012

Subramanian A et al. (2005). Gene set enrichment analysis. PNAS 102:15545-15550. doi:10.1073/pnas.0506580102

Examples

set.seed(1)
genes <- paste0("G", 1:200)
exwas <- S4Vectors::DataFrame(gene = genes, celltype = "Mono",
    exposure = "PM2.5",
    statistic = c(stats::rnorm(20, mean = 3), stats::rnorm(180)))
gene_sets <- list(shifted = genes[1:20], random = sample(genes, 25))
if (requireNamespace("fgsea", quietly = TRUE)) {
    run_gsea(exwas, gene_sets, min_size = 10L)
}
#> DataFrame with 2 rows and 11 columns
#>       pathway        pval        padj   log2err        ES       NES      size
#>   <character>   <numeric>   <numeric> <numeric> <numeric> <numeric> <integer>
#> 1      random 5.72581e-01 5.72581e-01  0.165657 -0.255891 -0.917942        25
#> 2     shifted 9.36476e-17 1.87295e-16  1.057464  0.965471  2.378020        20
#>              leadingEdge    celltype    exposure padj_global
#>              <character> <character> <character>   <numeric>
#> 1 G141;G168;G35;G97;G7..        Mono       PM2.5 5.72581e-01
#> 2 G4;G11;G15;G18;G19;G..        Mono       PM2.5 1.87295e-16
